title: How to stay calm when you know you'll be stressed
speaker: Daniel Levitin

sentences.en: A few years ago, I broke into my own house.
sentences.zh: 几年前,我闯进了自己的房子

sentences.en: I had just driven home, it was around midnight in the dead of Montreal winter, I had been visiting my friend, Jeff, across town, and the thermometer on the front porch read minus 40 degrees -- and don't bother asking if that's Celsius or Fahrenheit,
sentences.zh: 我刚刚开车回家 就在蒙特利尔冬天的午夜左右 我拜访了我的朋友Jeff 穿过镇子 前面门廊的温度计读了零下40度

sentences.en: minus 40 is where the two scales meet -- it was very cold.
sentences.zh: 零下40是两个比例相交的地方-- 当时非常寒冷。

sentences.en: And as I stood on the front porch fumbling in my pockets, I found I didn't have my keys.
sentences.zh: 当我站在前门的门廊上 口袋里翻滚, 我发现我没有我的钥匙。

sentences.en: In fact, I could see them through the window, lying on the dining room table where I had left them.
sentences.zh: 事实上,我可以从窗户看到他们 躺在我离开的餐桌上

sentences.en: So I quickly ran around and tried all the other doors and windows, and they were locked tight.
sentences.zh: 所以我迅速跑来跑去 尝试了所有其他的门和窗子, 他们被紧紧锁住。

sentences.en: I thought about calling a locksmith -- at least I had my cellphone, but at midnight, it could take a while for a locksmith to show up, and it was cold.
sentences.zh: 我想打电话给锁匠—— 至少我有我的手机, 但是在午夜,它可能需要一段时间 一个锁匠出现, 和它的寒冷。

sentences.en: I couldn't go back to my friend Jeff's house for the night because I had an early flight to Europe the next morning, and I needed to get my passport and my suitcase.
sentences.zh: 我不能回朋友杰夫家过夜 因为我第二天早上有早班机去欧洲 我需要拿护照和行李箱

sentences.en: So, desperate and freezing cold, I found a large rock and I broke through the basement window, cleared out the shards of glass, I crawled through, I found a piece of cardboard and taped it up over the opening,
sentences.zh: 所以,绝望和寒冷, 我发现一个大石头 打破了地下室的窗户, 清除了玻璃碎片, 我爬过, 我找到一块纸板 并把它贴在开口上,

sentences.en: figuring that in the morning, on the way to the airport, I could call my contractor and ask him to fix it.
sentences.zh: 早上去机场的路上 我打电话给承包商 叫他修好它

sentences.en: This was going to be expensive, but probably no more expensive than a middle-of-the-night locksmith, so I figured, under the circumstances, I was coming out even.
sentences.zh: 这将是昂贵的, 但也许没有什么比 半夜锁匠更昂贵, 所以我想,在这样的情况下, 我出来了。

sentences.en: Now, I'm a neuroscientist by training and I know a little bit about how the brain performs under stress.
sentences.zh: 现在,我是一个神经科学家 通过训练,我知道一点点 关于大脑如何在压力下表现。

sentences.en: It releases cortisol that raises your heart rate, it modulates adrenaline levels and it clouds your thinking.
sentences.zh: 它释放了高心率的皮质醇 调节了肾上腺素水平 使你的思维蒙上阴影

sentences.en: So the next morning, when I woke up on too little sleep, worrying about the hole in the window, and a mental note that I had to call my contractor, and the freezing temperatures, and the meetings I had upcoming in Europe,
sentences.zh: 第二天早上,当我醒来时 睡眠太少了, 担心窗户的洞, 以及我不得不打电话给我的承包商, 和寒冷的温度, 和会议,我即将在欧洲,

sentences.en: and, you know, with all the cortisol in my brain, my thinking was cloudy, but I didn't know it was cloudy because my thinking was cloudy.
sentences.zh: 而且,你知道,在我脑中所有的皮质醇, 我的想法是阴云, 但我不知道它是阴云 因为我的想法是阴云。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And it wasn't until I got to the airport check-in counter, that I realized I didn't have my passport.
sentences.zh: 直到我到机场报到柜台 我才意识到我没有护照

sentences.en: (Laughter) So I raced home in the snow and ice, 40 minutes, got my passport, raced back to the airport, I made it just in time, but they had given away my seat to someone else,
sentences.zh: 我骑着雪和冰回家,40分钟, 拿到我的护照, 赛车回到机场, 我及时赶到了, 但是他们把我的座位给了别人,

sentences.en: so I got stuck in the back of the plane, next to the bathrooms, in a seat that wouldn't recline, on an eight-hour flight.
sentences.zh: 所以我被困在飞机的后面, 旁边的浴室, 在一个座位上,不会 直线,在8小时的飞行。

sentences.en: Well, I had a lot of time to think during those eight hours and no sleep.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我有很多时间 思考在这八个小时 而不睡觉。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And I started wondering, are there things that I can do, systems that I can put into place, that will prevent bad things from happening?
sentences.zh: 我开始想,我能做点什么, 建立一些能防止坏事发生的系统吗?

sentences.en: Or at least if bad things happen, will minimize the likelihood of it being a total catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 或至少如果发生坏事, 将降低它成为一场大灾难的可能性。

sentences.en: So I started thinking about that, but my thoughts didn't crystallize until about a month later.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始想这个, 但我的想法直到一个月后才变得结实。

sentences.en: I was having dinner with my colleague, Danny Kahneman, the Nobel Prize winner, and I somewhat embarrassedly told him about having broken my window, and, you know, forgotten my passport, and Danny shared with me that he'd been practicing something called prospective hindsight.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同事Danny Kahneman共进晚餐, 诺贝尔奖得主, 我有点尴尬地告诉他 打破了我的窗户,

sentences.en: (Laughter) It's something that he had gotten from the psychologist Gary Klein, who had written about it a few years before, also called the pre-mortem.
sentences.zh: 这是他从心理学家Gary Klein那里得到的, 他几年前写过这个故事, 也叫验尸前。

sentences.en: Now, you all know what the postmortem is.
sentences.zh: 现在,你们都知道死后是什么

sentences.en: Whenever there's a disaster, a team of experts come in and they try to figure out what went wrong, right?
sentences.zh: 每当发生灾难, 一组专家进来 他们试图找出 出了什么问题,对不对?

sentences.en: Well, in the pre-mortem, Danny explained, you look ahead and you try to figure out all the things that could go wrong, and then you try to figure out what you can do to prevent those things from happening, or to minimize the damage.
sentences.zh: 在验尸前 Danny解释过 你向前看 试着找出所有可能出错的事 然后你试着想出你能做些什么来防止那些事发生 或者尽可能减少伤害

sentences.en: So what I want to talk to you about today are some of the things we can do in the form of a pre-mortem.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想和你们谈的 是我们可以用验尸前的形式 做的一些事情

sentences.en: Some of them are obvious, some of them are not so obvious.
sentences.zh: 有些是显而易见的,有些不是那么明显。

sentences.en: I'll start with the obvious ones. Around the home, designate a place for things that are easily lost.
sentences.zh: 我从明显的东西开始 在家里 指定一个容易丢失的东西的地方

sentences.en: Now, this sounds like common sense, and it is, but there's a lot of science to back this up, based on the way our spatial memory works.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像常识,它是, 但有很多科学 支持这一点, 以我们的空间记忆方式。

sentences.en: There's a structure in the brain called the hippocampus, that evolved over tens of thousands of years, to keep track of the locations of important things -- where the well is, where fish can be found,
sentences.zh: 大脑里有一个结构叫做河马坎普斯, 它经过数万年的进化, 来追踪重要事物的位置-- 井在哪里,可以找到鱼,

sentences.en: that stand of fruit trees, where the friendly and enemy tribes live.
sentences.zh: 那里是果树的摊子 友好的和敌人的部落都住在那里

sentences.en: The hippocampus is the part of the brain that in London taxicab drivers becomes enlarged.
sentences.zh: 河马坎普斯是大脑的一部分 在伦敦,出租车司机会变大。

sentences.en: It's the part of the brain that allows squirrels to find their nuts.
sentences.zh: 这是大脑的一部分 允许松鼠发现他们的坚果。

sentences.en: And if you're wondering, somebody actually did the experiment where they cut off the olfactory sense of the squirrels, and they could still find their nuts.
sentences.zh: 如果你想知道,有人实际上做了实验 他们切断了松鼠的嗅觉, 他们仍然可以找到他们的坚果。

sentences.en: They weren't using smell, they were using the hippocampus, this exquisitely evolved mechanism in the brain for finding things.
sentences.zh: 他们没有使用气味, 他们使用河马坎普斯, 这种精致的进化机制 在大脑中发现的东西。

sentences.en: But it's really good for things that don't move around much, not so good for things that move around.
sentences.zh: 但它真的好的东西 不移动很多, 不太好的东西 移动。

sentences.en: So this is why we lose car keys and reading glasses and passports.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们失去了车钥匙 和阅读眼镜和护照。

sentences.en: So in the home, designate a spot for your keys -- a hook by the door, maybe a decorative bowl.
sentences.zh: 所以在家里,给钥匙指定一个位置 -- 门边的钩子,也许一个装饰性的碗。

sentences.en: For your passport, a particular drawer. For your reading glasses, a particular table.
sentences.zh: 护照 抽屉 眼镜 桌子

sentences.en: If you designate a spot and you're scrupulous about it, your things will always be there when you look for them.
sentences.zh: 如果你指定一个地点 并且你小心翼翼的, 你的东西将永远在那里 当你寻找他们。

sentences.en: What about travel? Take a cell phone picture of your credit cards, your driver's license, your passport, mail it to yourself so it's in the cloud.
sentences.zh: 旅行呢 拿着你的信用卡 驾照 护照 寄给自己

sentences.en: If these things are lost or stolen, you can facilitate replacement.
sentences.zh: 如果这些东西丢失或被盗,你可以帮助替换。

sentences.en: Now these are some rather obvious things.
sentences.zh: 现在,这些是一些相当明显的事物。

sentences.en: Remember, when you're under stress, the brain releases cortisol.
sentences.zh: 记住 当你承受压力时 大脑会释放皮质素

sentences.en: Cortisol is toxic, and it causes cloudy thinking.
sentences.zh: Cortisol 有毒, 并引起阴云思考。

sentences.en: So part of the practice of the pre-mortem is to recognize that under stress you're not going to be at your best, and you should put systems in place.
sentences.zh: 验尸前的部分实践就是 承认在压力下 你不会是最好的, 你应该设置系统。

sentences.en: And there's perhaps no more stressful a situation than when you're confronted with a medical decision to make.
sentences.zh: 也许没有比面对医疗决定 更紧张的情况了

sentences.en: And at some point, all of us are going to be in that position, where we have to make a very important decision about the future of our medical care or that of a loved one, to help them with a decision.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候,我们所有人都会处于这种地位, 我们必须对我们未来的医疗或者亲人的未来做出一个非常重要的决定, 帮助他们做出一个决定。

sentences.en: And so I want to talk about that. And I'm going to talk about a very particular medical condition.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谈谈这个问题。我要谈谈一个非常特别的医疗状况。

sentences.en: But this stands as a proxy for all kinds of medical decision-making, and indeed for financial decision-making, and social decision-making -- any kind of decision you have to make that would benefit from a rational assessment of the facts.
sentences.zh: 但这代表了各种医疗决策,实际上也代表了金融决策,以及社会决策 -- -- 任何你必须做出的决定 -- -- 都会受益于对事实的合理评估。

sentences.en: So suppose you go to your doctor and the doctor says, "I just got your lab work back, your cholesterol's a little high."
sentences.zh: 所以假设你去看你的医生 医生说,"我刚刚得到了你的实验室工作, 你的胆固醇有点高。"

sentences.en: Now, you all know that high cholesterol is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, heart attack, stroke.
sentences.zh: 你们都知道高胆固醇 与心血管疾病、心脏病发作、中风的风险增加有关

sentences.en: And so you're thinking having high cholesterol isn't the best thing, and so the doctor says, "You know, I'd like to give you a drug that will help you lower your cholesterol, a statin."
sentences.zh: 所以你认为高胆固醇不是最好的事情, 所以医生说,“你知道,我想给你一种药 来帮助你降低胆固醇, 一种凝固剂。”

sentences.en: And you've probably heard of statins, you know that they're among the most widely prescribed drugs in the world today, you probably even know people who take them.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过Stains, 你知道他们是世界上 最广泛的处方药物之一, 你可能甚至知道谁服用它们。

sentences.en: And so you're thinking, "Yeah! Give me the statin."
sentences.zh: 所以你在想,“是的,把Statin给我。”

sentences.en: But there's a question you should ask at this point, a statistic you should ask for that most doctors don't like talking about, and pharmaceutical companies like talking about even less.
sentences.zh: 但是现在你应该问一个问题, 一个你应该问的统计数字, 大部分医生不喜欢谈论, 制药公司喜欢谈论更少。

sentences.en: It's for the number needed to treat. Now, what is this, the NNT?
sentences.zh: 这是要治疗的号码 这是什么 NNT?

sentences.en: It's the number of people that need to take a drug or undergo a surgery or any medical procedure before one person is helped.
sentences.zh: 这是需要服用药物或接受手术或任何医疗程序的人数 才能帮助一个人。

sentences.en: And you're thinking, what kind of crazy statistic is that?
sentences.zh: 你在想,这算什么疯狂的统计数字?

sentences.en: The number should be one. My doctor wouldn't prescribe something to me if it's not going to help.
sentences.zh: 号码应该是一号,我医生不会开药给我的

sentences.en: But actually, medical practice doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 但实际上 医学实践不是那样的

sentences.en: And it's not the doctor's fault, if it's anybody's fault, it's the fault of scientists like me.
sentences.zh: 这不是医生的错, 如果这是任何人的错, 这是科学家的错,像我这样的。

sentences.en: We haven't figured out the underlying mechanisms well enough.
sentences.zh: 我们还没弄清楚底线

sentences.en: But GlaxoSmithKline estimates that 90 percent of the drugs work in only 30 to 50 percent of the people.
sentences.zh: 但GlaxoSmithKline估计 90%的毒品 只在30%到50%的人中起作用。

sentences.en: So the number needed to treat for the most widely prescribed statin, what do you suppose it is?
sentences.zh: 那么治疗最广泛处方的Stain需要多少? 你觉得是什么?

sentences.en: How many people have to take it before one person is helped?
sentences.zh: 在一个人得到帮助之前 有多少人要接受它?

sentences.en: 300. This is according to research by research practitioners Jerome Groopman and Pamela Hartzband, independently confirmed by Bloomberg.com.
sentences.zh: 300. 根据研究实践者杰罗姆·格罗普曼和帕梅拉·哈茨班德的研究,这一点得到Bloomberg.com的独立证实。

sentences.en: I ran through the numbers myself. 300 people have to take the drug for a year before one heart attack, stroke or other adverse event is prevented.
sentences.zh: 我亲自查过号码 300人得服用一年 才能预防心脏病发作 中风或其他不良事件

sentences.en: Now you're probably thinking, "Well, OK, one in 300 chance of lowering my cholesterol.
sentences.zh: 现在你大概在想, "好吧,三百分之一的机会 降低我的胆固醇。

sentences.en: Why not, doc? Give me the prescription anyway."
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢,医生?

sentences.en: But you should ask at this point for another statistic, and that is, "Tell me about the side effects." Right?
sentences.zh: 但你现在应该问另一个统计数字, 那就是,"告诉我副作用",对吗?

sentences.en: So for this particular drug, the side effects occur in five percent of the patients.
sentences.zh: 对于这种特殊的药物 副作用发生在5%的病人身上

sentences.en: And they include terrible things -- debilitating muscle and joint pain, gastrointestinal distress -- but now you're thinking, "Five percent, not very likely it's going to happen to me, I'll still take the drug."
sentences.zh: 它们包括可怕的事情—— 肌肉衰弱和关节疼痛,胃肠溃疡—— 现在你在想,“五分之一, 可能不会发生在我身上, 我还是会吃药。”

sentences.en: But wait a minute. Remember under stress you're not thinking clearly.
sentences.zh: 等等 记住压力下你没想清楚

sentences.en: So think about how you're going to work through this ahead of time, so you don't have to manufacture the chain of reasoning on the spot.
sentences.zh: 所以先想想你会如何度过这个难关 这样你就不用当场制造推理链了

sentences.en: 300 people take the drug, right? One person's helped, five percent of those 300 have side effects, that's 15 people.
sentences.zh: 300人服用了药物,对吧?

sentences.en: You're 15 times more likely to be harmed by the drug than you are to be helped by the drug.
sentences.zh: 你受毒品伤害的可能性比受毒品伤害的可能性高15倍

sentences.en: Now, I'm not saying whether you should take the statin or not.
sentences.zh: 现在,我不是说 你是否应该采取statin。

sentences.en: I'm just saying you should have this conversation with your doctor.
sentences.zh: 我只是说 你该跟你的医生谈谈

sentences.en: Medical ethics requires it, it's part of the principle of informed consent.
sentences.zh: 医疗道德要求它, 这是知情同意原则的一部分。

sentences.en: You have the right to have access to this kind of information to begin the conversation about whether you want to take the risks or not.
sentences.zh: 你有权接触这种信息 开始谈论你是否愿意冒风险

sentences.en: Now you might be thinking I've pulled this number out of the air for shock value, but in fact it's rather typical, this number needed to treat.
sentences.zh: 现在你们可能认为我已经把这个数字从空气中调出 以达到冲击值, 但事实上这是非常典型的, 这个数字需要治疗。

sentences.en: For the most widely performed surgery on men over the age of 50, removal of the prostate for cancer, the number needed to treat is 49.
sentences.zh: 50岁以上男子进行的最广泛的手术,除去癌症前列腺,治疗需要49人。

sentences.en: That's right, 49 surgeries are done for every one person who's helped.
sentences.zh: 对,每个被帮助的人 都会接受49次手术

sentences.en: And the side effects in that case occur in 50 percent of the patients.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下,副作用 发生在50%的病人。

sentences.en: They include impotence, erectile dysfunction, urinary incontinence, rectal tearing, fecal incontinence.
sentences.zh: 其中包括无能、勃起功能障碍、尿不自禁、直肠撕裂、失禁。

sentences.en: And if you're lucky, and you're one of the 50 percent who has these, they'll only last for a year or two.
sentences.zh: 如果你是幸运的, 你是50%的人之一 谁拥有这些, 他们只会持续一两年。

sentences.en: So the idea of the pre-mortem is to think ahead of time to the questions that you might be able to ask that will push the conversation forward.
sentences.zh: 因此,验尸前的想法是 提前思考 你可能能够问的问题 将会推动对话向前推进。

sentences.en: You don't want to have to manufacture all of this on the spot.
sentences.zh: 你不会非得当场制造这些的

sentences.en: And you also want to think about things like quality of life.
sentences.zh: 你也想想想生活品质

sentences.en: Because you have a choice oftentimes, do you I want a shorter life that's pain-free, or a longer life that might have a great deal of pain towards the end?
sentences.zh: 因为你有选择 经常,你想要 较短的寿命,这是没有痛苦的, 还是更长的寿命, 可能会有很大的痛苦 最终?

sentences.en: These are things to talk about and think about now, with your family and your loved ones.
sentences.zh: 这些都是现在要谈和思考的事情, 和你的家人和你爱的人。

sentences.en: You might change your mind in the heat of the moment, but at least you're practiced with this kind of thinking.
sentences.zh: 你可能会改变你的想法 在当时的热, 但至少你练习 这种想法。

sentences.en: Remember, our brain under stress releases cortisol, and one of the things that happens at that moment is a whole bunch on systems shut down.
sentences.zh: 记住,我们的大脑在压力下释放 皮质醇, 并且其中之一 发生的事情 在那一刻是 一整堆 在系统关闭。

sentences.en: There's an evolutionary reason for this.
sentences.zh: 这是进化的原因

sentences.en: Face-to-face with a predator, you don't need your digestive system, or your libido, or your immune system, because if you're body is expending metabolism on those things and you don't react quickly, you might become the lion's lunch, and then none of those things matter.
sentences.zh: 和捕食者面对面, 你不需要你的消化系统, 或你的性欲, 或你的免疫系统, 因为如果你的身体是 将新陈代谢花在这些东西上 而且你不反应快, 你可能会成为狮子的午餐, 然后这些事情都无关紧要。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, one of the things that goes out the window during those times of stress is rational, logical thinking, as Danny Kahneman and his colleagues have shown.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是,在压力时期走出窗户的一件事是理性的、合乎逻辑的思维,正如Danny Kahneman和他的同事所显示的那样。

sentences.en: So we need to train ourselves to think ahead to these kinds of situations.
sentences.zh: 因此,我们需要自我训练,以先入为主地思考这种局势。

sentences.en: I think the important point here is recognizing that all of us are flawed.
sentences.zh: 我认为,这里的重要一点是认识到我们所有人都有缺陷。

sentences.en: We all are going to fail now and then. The idea is to think ahead to what those failures might be, to put systems in place that will help minimize the damage, or to prevent the bad things from happening in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我们都会不时失败。 我们的想法是先考虑一下这些失败可能是什么,建立有助于尽可能减少破坏的系统,或者首先防止坏事发生。

sentences.en: Getting back to that snowy night in Montreal, when I got back from my trip, I had my contractor install a combination lock next to the door, with a key to the front door in it, an easy to remember combination.
sentences.zh: 回到蒙特利尔的雪天之夜 当我回来旅行时 我的承包商在门边安装了一个组合锁 里面有前门的钥匙 很容易记起来的组合

sentences.en: And I have to admit, I still have piles of mail that haven't been sorted, and piles of emails that I haven't gone through.
sentences.zh: 我不得不承认,我仍然有一堆邮件 还没有整理, 和一堆邮件,我没有经过。

sentences.en: So I'm not completely organized, but I see organization as a gradual process, and I'm getting there.
sentences.zh: 所以,我并不是完全有组织, 但我认为组织是一个渐进的过程, 我得到了。

sentences.en: Thank you very much. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。 （掌声）
